facts.fact: According to Bolt's documentation, short, common words are typically one token each, while longer or less common words can be several tokens.
facts.quote: Short, common words are typically one token each, but longer or less common words can be several.

facts.fact: Bolt's documentation states that every prompt submitted in Build mode updates the code and uses tokens, while Plan mode uses fewer tokens because it makes no changes to the project.
facts.quote: In Build mode, every prompt you submit updates your code and uses tokens, but Plan mode uses fewer tokens because it doesn’t make any changes to your project.

facts.fact: Bolt's documentation states that clicking an on-screen button or built-in action does not use tokens, whereas prompting Bolt does.
facts.quote: Clicking an on-screen button or action doesn’t use tokens, but prompting Bolt does.

facts.fact: Bolt's documentation says the Standard agent gives accurate results for tasks of average complexity without the additional token cost of deeper reasoning.
facts.quote: For tasks of average complexity, the Standard agent gives you accurate results without the additional token cost of deeper reasoning.

facts.fact: Bolt's documentation says the Max agent uses more tokens to work through the full scope of complex tasks, and that using it for straightforward tasks may use more tokens than necessary.
facts.quote: For more complex tasks, the Max agent uses more tokens to work through the full scope of your task.

facts.fact: Bolt's documentation states that adding information to Bolt's context from connectors increases token consumption, and recommends turning on connectors for a project only when needed.
facts.quote: adding information to Bolt’s context increases token consumption. We recommend turning on connectors for a project only when you need them.

facts.fact: Bolt's documentation notes that each automatic error fix attempt uses tokens, so repeatedly clicking Attempt fix consumes more tokens.
facts.quote: remember that each attempt uses tokens.

facts.fact: Bolt's documentation states that Bolt processes fewer tokens when it has less context to process, so keeping context low improves both performance and token efficiency.
facts.quote: Bolt processes fewer tokens when it has less context to process, so keeping your context low improves both performance and token efficiency.
